//: Foundry ADOPTER PROJECT INVENTORY + the meta-repo MANIFEST (the WHAT, workspace-side). Generic foundry/ primitives resolve project-specifics (repo paths, boot command, conventions, live-seam drivers) from HERE rather than hardcoding them. This is ALSO the multi-repo control-center manifest: to host an infra/service repo as a gitignored sibling subdir, add it under repos{} keyed by a target_repo dispatch key — see docs/SETUP.md 'Multi-repo control center'. Seeded self-only (path '.') so a fresh, un-populated workspace stays DOCTOR-GREEN; add hosted entries live, only once the repo is cloned. Captured + updated by /foundry:init. Sibling of .claude/foundry-operators.json (identity). RULE: never bake a project-specific value into a foundry/ primitive — reference this file by key.

project.name: REPLACE-ME
project.description: REPLACE-ME — one line: what this project is, who it's for. (This workspace is the control center; the product/infra repos it builds are hosted as gitignored siblings, see repos{} + docs/SETUP.md.)

workspace.role: the control center itself (the WHAT — specs, governance, the manifest). Self entry: resolves to the workspace root, so the doctor treats this as a single-repo adopter until a hosted repo is added.

repos.//hosted-repo-example: To host an infra/service repo, add a sibling entry once you've cloned it into the gitignored subdir, e.g.: "infra": { "path": "infra", "kind": "infra-repo", "role": "the project's IaC (OpenTofu/Kubernetes)" }. The key is the target_repo dispatch key. Runbook: docs/SETUP.md 'Multi-repo control center'.

surfaces.//: §22.4b app-exercise binding: surface kind -> how a live-seam human-equivalent walk exercises it (the generic analog of 'make dev + Chrome MCP'). /foundry:init captures this for your app; /foundry:doctor fail-closes if a code-profile contract declares a surface with no usable driver here.
